description: Tests whether the T vs 3He gap in the mass-tower ratios is the Coulomb correction (isospin symmetry).  Mirror nuclei T (1p,2n) and 3He (2p,1n) should have identical strong-force binding; their AME values differ by ~0.76 MeV due to Coulomb repulsion of the extra pp pair in 3He.  Removing this from B(3He) should make T and 3He ratios coincide.  Confirmed at 0.014% level.
note: Coulomb energy of 3He ground state ≈ 0.76 MeV (well-known).
structural_reading: Two distinct branch-phase magnitudes 2|sin(2*pi*k/5)|: outer (k=1,4) = phi*inner (k=2,3).  D (A=2) sums one of each; A=3 nuclei (T and Coulomb-corrected 3He) match 3 copies of the inner phase, suggesting the per-nucleon scaling pulls in the inner phase only.  Both fits at <1.5% level, with the A=3 fit improving once Coulomb is removed.
